verses.1: And it happened that David and his men arrived at Ziklag on the third day. Amalek’s people attacked Ziklag. They burned down Ziklag with fire.
verses.2: And they let the women who had been with them from childhood until adulthood live freely. No one was killed. They continued to go their own ways.
verses.3: And David and his men came to the city. There they saw that the city was in flames; its women, children, and girls were all dead.
verses.4: And David and the people who were with him raised their voices in praise, even though they didn’t have the strength to continue singing.
verses.5: And the two daughters of David lay down together: Ahinoam and Abigail, the wives of Nabal from Carmel.
verses.6: David was made great by God. For the people said to Saul, “He is a man who will bring ruin upon all of us, both his sons and daughters.” But David became stronger in the eyes of God.
verses.7: And David said to Abiathar, the priest, son of Achimolech. “Please give me that censer.” So Abiathar brought the censer to David.
verses.8: And David asked the Lord, “Let me follow this great man.” But the Lord said to him, “Follow him, but remember that you must also be strong yourself.”
verses.9: And David went out, along with six men with him. They arrived at the river Besor. The remaining people stood there.
verses.10: And David pursued them, along with four thousand men. They stood at the banks of the river Besor.
verses.11: And they found a Egyptian man in the field. They took him to David, gave him some bread to eat, and he drank water from the river.
verses.12: They gave him bread and two kinds of meat to eat. His hunger was satisfied, for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
verses.13: And David said to him, “Who are you, and where do you come from?” The young man from Egypt replied, “I am a servant of the king of Amalek. My master abandoned me because I was sick today.”
verses.14: We have stripped off the skin from the rock. And on that rock, we burned all the bones and carcases.
verses.15: And David said to him, “Please take me to this king.” He replied, “I will do it for you, if you kill me and hand me over to my enemy, and then I will bring you to that king.”
verses.16: And he went up, and behold, they were eating and drinking, and rejoicing in all the great abundance that had been taken from the land of Philistines and from the land of Judah.
verses.17: David camped there from dawn until evening. No one escaped from them, except for four thousand young men who rode on donkeys and fled.
verses.18: David saved all that Amalek had taken, as well as his two wives. David saved them all.
verses.19: And David did not take anything from them, neither from the small nor the great, neither from sons nor daughters, nor from slaves, nor from anything else that they had. He gave them back everything.
verses.20: David took all the sheep with him. In the morning, they went ahead of the goods. And they said, “This is David’s spoil.”
verses.21: David went to the people who had rebelled against King David. He brought them back to the Valley of Hinnom. Then he went out to meet David and the people. David asked them to return to him, asking for forgiveness.
verses.22: And every evil person refused to do this, without any exception. But those who went with David said, “Since they didn’t go with me, then I won’t give them any part of the spoils that we captured. It’s like if someone were to take away his wife and children, and then still continue to live their lives as usual.”
verses.23: And David said, “Do not do this, my brothers. For God has given us these things, and He has protected us. So, do not take away what He has given us.”
verses.24: And who will listen to you when you say this? For those who are on the battlefield and those who are in charge of the food supply, they will also be taken captive together.
verses.25: And from that day on, it became a law and a rule for Israel, until today.
verses.26: And David went to Ziklag. He sent out a message to the elders of Judah, saying, “Here is a blessing from God for you, from the spoils taken from the enemies of Jehovah.”
verses.27: In the house of El, and in the heights of Negeb, and in Yatir.
verses.28: And when it is in chaos, and when it is in confusion, and when it is in destruction.
verses.29: And in the cities of my God’s mercy, and in the cities of Kinnim.
verses.30: And when in the wilderness, and when in the smoke-filled places, and when at the time of darkness.
